item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo suspended for 30 days after quitting Portugal camp
item.description: On 30 September, the former Real Madrid and Manchester United star walked out of an international camp before a training session at Parken Stadium in Copenhagen.

item.title: Deadly floods sweep through eastern Spain after torrential rain
item.description: Torrential rain triggered severe flooding in eastern Spain, sweeping away cars, submerging roads and leaving at least four people dead.

item.title: Rubio puts Trans-Caspian trade and critical minerals at centre of Central Asia talks
item.description: The US and five Central Asian governments backed closer transport and industrial cooperation at a C5+1 meeting in Samarkand. Rubio also held bilateral talks, while Uzbekistan signed the Artemis Accords.

item.title: Lavrov backs Iran, hours after Trump says Russia doing 'very little' to help Tehran
item.description: Just hours after Trump publicly claimed Russia was doing “little” to help Iran, Moscow reaffirmed its full support for Tehran, with Foreign Minister Lavrov describing Iran's fight as a "just cause."

item.title: 'How are we supposed to recover?': Shopkeepers react to looting and destruction across France
item.description: French shopkeepers are struggling to come to terms with the destruction left by a night of rioting and looting, with some fearing for the future of their businesses and employees.

item.title: Albanian PM Rama accuses anti-government protesters of crossing 'red line' amid violent demonstrations
item.description: The European Commission released a statement condemning the violence in Albania on Sunday, saying it had "no place in a democratic society" and that the response "must remain within the law and proportionate."

item.title: Macron increasingly isolated amid unrest across France
item.description: Saturday’s violent protests and looting across France have deepened Macron’s political isolation, raising questions over his authority.

item.title: Trump signs order aimed at boosting women’s health research
item.description: United States President Donald Trump signed an executive order establishing two bodies to boost women’s health research, address gaps in medical knowledge and improve prevention, diagnosis and treatment.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 19th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 19th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Dutch PM Rob Jetten and partner expecting child via surrogate mother: 'Someone very special is on the way'
item.description: "Being a surrogate mother feels like a very special way to help make our dear friends’ dream come true," Lisa, the surrogate mother, was quoted as saying.

item.title: Qatar plans new defence partnership and warns of energy crisis 'peak'
item.description: Qatar is preparing a new regional defence partnership while keeping channels open with Tehran, arguing that dialogue and economic ties offer a route to lasting peace. Doha also warned of an energy disruption “peak” with more difficulties on the horizon “in the coming days and months”.

item.title: EU Parliament leaders set for re-election despite cracks in centrist alliance
item.description: Manfred Weber, Iratxe García Pérez and Valérie Hayer are expected to be re-elected unopposed, even as growing tensions threaten the centrist alliance supporting Ursula von der Leyen.

item.title: France galvanised by shopkeepers and locals who fought back against rioters and looters
item.description: Social media videos of French shopkeepers and locals taking matters into their own hands and fighting back against rioters have seen an outpouring of public support and solidarity.

item.title: Euronews press review: French newspapers dissect weekend of unrest and rioting
item.description: French newspapers examine the causes of a weekend of unrest, questioning the police response, violence and examining the role of the ultra-left.

item.title: Musk pledges SpaceX shares to every US child in potential $10.7bn giveaway
item.description: Elon Musk says he will give one SpaceX share to every child in America next year, a pledge worth about $10.7bn (€9.5bn) at Friday’s closing price. He has yet to explain who would qualify or how the shares would be distributed.

item.title: Norway to extend proposed under-16 social media ban to online games and messaging apps
item.description: Online games and messaging services were initially expected to receive broad exemptions, but the government has now decided to assess platforms based on their potential risks to children.

item.title: Could France’s debt troubles tip Italy into recession?
item.description: Rising borrowing costs and political uncertainty are putting France’s finances under pressure. Oxford Economics warns that a severe bond-market shock could push both France and Italy into recession in 2027, although a debt crisis remains outside its central forecast.

item.title: Visegrad Four urge Brussels to ease Russian energy phase-out rules
item.description: The group is calling on Brussels for more funding to cope with the end of Russian energy imports in 2027, amid high electricity prices across Europe.

item.title: Professional chefs coach amateur cooks in French boxing glove cooking competition
item.description: Professional chefs had just 20 minutes to guide their amateur teammates through making a soufflé omelette, without using their hands to help.

item.title: France announces partial curfews after weekend of violence
item.description: It comes after cost-of-living protests descended into widespread violence and looting across France on Saturday. Clashes with police also continued on Sunday in some parts of the country.

item.title: Protesters block entrances to Paris’s Louvre museum
item.description: Demonstrators blocked the entrances to the Louvre in Paris on Monday, as tensions remained high following a weekend of protests, clashes and looting in France.

item.title: 'We won't let this continue': French PM orders local curfews after weekend unrest
item.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has ordered localised, partial curfews in some urban areas following a weekend of rioting and looting across France.

item.title: UN food agency to cut aid to 500,000 people in Gaza as funding dries up
item.description: Families who keep their support will get smaller rations and less cash, even though two-thirds of the territory’s population still needs help to survive.

item.title: New Chinese brands drive curiosity at the Mondial de l'Auto car show in Paris
item.description: Half a million visitors flocked to Paris for the Mondial de l'Auto, with the presence of new Chinese brands drawing large crowds of curious European car fans.

item.title: France launches ‘massive’ law enforcement operation after weekend looting, PM says
item.description: Lecornu said nearly 200 investigators would analyse footage from the weekend to identify suspects in the Paris region alone after businesses were destroyed and looted after protests turned violent on Saturday.

item.title: Tents fill Lisbon square as protesters highlight Portugal’s housing crisis
item.description: Protesters camped overnight in central Lisbon over the weekend to denounce Portugal’s housing crisis, as soaring rents leave many struggling to afford accommodation.

item.title: EU plans March summit in Rome as Italy eyes early election
item.description: The EU is preparing to hold its March 2027 summit in Rome to mark the 70th anniversary of the Treaties of Rome, subject to unanimous approval, as Italy faces the prospect of an early spring election.

item.title: Ebola: Kenya confirms eighth case as DRC outbreak reaches new province
item.description: Kenya has confirmed an eighth Ebola case, while the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to spread to new areas.

item.title: Montenegro moves to settle Croatia disputes threatening its EU membership bid
item.description: Montenegro has moved to address Croatia’s wartime grievances as it seeks to keep its EU accession bid on track for 2028, amid growing pressure from Germany for a swift resolution.

item.title: German police say two men turned themselves in after smashing car into airport fence
item.description: In August, an attack with an explosives-laden drone took place at the same airport. German authorities blamed that on Russia, an allegation denied by Moscow.

item.title: From 'Werwulf' to a 1930s Batman: Key takeways from Robert Eggers masterclass at Lumière
item.description: A world exclusive for 'Werwulf', talk of Lily-Rose Depp's eyes, and the enduring horror of Ridley Scott's 'Alien'... Director Robert Eggers treats audiences at Lyon's Lumière Film Festival.

item.title: Istanbul flood death toll rises to eight as rescuers find more bodies, governor says
item.description: Authorities have received nearly 20,000 reports about property damage as a result of the torrential rainfall and the resulting floods, Governor Davut Gül said.

item.title: US issues rare Middle East red alert warning to its citizens in the region
item.description: Washington has taken the rare measure to issue a red alert to US citizens in 12 countries across the Middle East, citing risks of potential attacks on US interests.

item.title: Roads and cars submerged as heavy rain floods eastern Spain
item.description: At least two people have died after heavy rain triggered flooding in eastern Spain. Streets and cars were submerged in the Valencia region as rescuers worked to evacuate stranded residents. Authorities urged people to stay indoors.

item.title: Daedalus: Greece unveils new supercomputer as it eyes role in Europe's AI race
item.description: With a performance of 85.69 petaflops, Daedalus opens up new possibilities for developing advanced AI models in Greece.

item.title: Northern Ireland and Scotland schools sent hoax bomb warnings, officials say
item.description: Meanwhile, Scottish police said "threatening messages" had also been sent to "a number of schools across Scotland".

item.title: Polish satellite maker Creotech Instruments plans tenfold capacity boost by 2029
item.description: CEO Grzegorz Brona warned that Europe could remain reliant on US rockets to launch its satellites into orbit for years.

item.title: Did an ancient Egyptian god inspire the Oscar statuette? A 2,700-year-old bronze offers a clue
item.description: A 2,700-year-old Egyptian statuette of the god Ptah, which recently sold at Frieze Masters in London, may hold a clue to the origin story of the Oscar statuette.

item.title: What do travellers want from AI? Room rates, not personalised itineraries, study says
item.description: Just 44% of travellers feel comfortable letting artificial intelligence plan out their holidays.

item.title: ‘Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres’: What does the French student protest slogan mean?
item.description: A Snapchat message, which students believe came from an undercover police officer, has become the rallying cry of a youth movement that has now spread to Belgium and Italy.

item.title: Lula supporters spell out his name in Rio waters before Brazil runoff
item.description: Brazil’s Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro clash in a tense debate over public spending, corruption and ties to the US, as polls show a tight 51–49 race.

item.title: Russia woos Asian tourists in attempt to counter European visits collapse
item.description: EU tourist arrivals fell from 5 million in 2019 to 160,000 in 2025 as sanctions, cancelled flights and other restrictions due to Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine severed Western leisure travel, prompting Moscow to look east.

item.title: Can European luxury brands still count on China for growth?
item.description: China’s shoppers are hunting for second-hand bargains and turning to homegrown brands, putting pressure on European luxury groups. China remains vital for luxury brands, but one analyst warns it may not drive growth over the next two to three years.

item.title: No Kings Day: Thousands rally across US against Trump
item.description: Thousands marched in US cities for a nationwide ‘No Kings’ protest against President Donald Trump, urging equal rights and early voting.

item.title: Von der Leyen, Costa head to Budapest in sign of EU-Hungary thaw
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa will join Hungarian PM Péter Magyar in Budapest on Friday to mark 70 years since the 1956 uprising, signalling a reset in EU-Hungary ties after Viktor Orbán’s years in power.

item.title: Mother leaves children on Poland mountain trail for 'whining', hikes to summit alone
item.description: Conditions on the trail were poor with a thick fog over the area, prompting shocked tourists to take care of the young boys.

item.title: EU eyes Arctic cable linking Greenland to Europe amid growing security threats
item.description: Brussels wants to secure digital infrastructure in the Arctic as melting ice and growing geopolitical tensions turn the polar region into a strategic corridor for trade, communications and security.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 19th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: 'We tore it up': French looters brag online as minister admits police 'lost control'
item.description: More than 2,000 shops were hit and the damage is put at hundreds of millions of euros, leaving the government to answer for its failure to see the violence coming.

item.title: Australian MP Helen Haines 'critically' hurt in car ramming attack, officials say
item.description: The 43-year-old male driver was detained by civilians, Mason said, and then arrested by police, who found a knife in his car.
